The petitioner has filed the present petition inter-alia praying as under:
"a. issue a writ in the nature of mandamus or any other writ/order/orders declaring the subject land being land admeasuring 15 acres situated in Village Bamnauli, Near Bijwasan, in the National Capital Territory of Delhi, New Delhi bearing khashra Nos.

(Old/New, with land measurements) as 350 (28/1) 4-16, 351 (28/10) 4-16, 352 (28/09) 4-16, 353 (28/02) 4-16, 331 (29/25) 2-19, 347 (29/15) 4-16, 346 (29/16)
2-00, 346 (26/16) 2-16, 348 (29/06) 4-16, 322 (29/7) 4-16, 323 (29/14) 4-16, 330 (29/17) 0-07, 330 (29/17) 5-17, 321 (29/8) 1-00, 324 (29/13) 1-00, 329 (29/18) 1-00,
354 (28/3) 4-16, 355 a 356 (28/8) 4-16, 358 (28/7) 4-13 6 359/1 (28/4) 3-06 to be out of the acquisition in view of the Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013,
the acquisition of the subject land be declared to be lapsed."

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the petitioner also pointed out that in the counter- affidavit filed on behalf of the Land Acquisition Collector (LAC) it is stated that the lands falling only in Khasra No.29/5/2/(2-17) were duly taken on the spot on 14.09.2007 by preparing possession proceedings and was handed over to the DDA on the spot.
It is stated that the notice dated 23.08.2007 under Section 12 (2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, was issued to the recorded owner but none had come forward to take the compensation.
4. The DDA has also filed a counter-affidavit stating that the possession of the land under reference has not been handed over to DDA by LAC/L&B.
The said counter-affidavit filed on behalf of DDA also indicates that possession of some land was taken over by DDA.
Prima facie, DDA could not have taken the possession of land, which has not been taken over by the LAC.

5. In view of the above, this court is prima facie satisfied that the possession of the subject land, save and except land falling in land comprising Khasra No.29/5/2/(2-17), has lapsed by virtue of the Section 24 (2) of the Right to Fair Compensation And Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation And Re-Settlement Act, 2013 as both the conditions viz. possession not having been taken over, and compensation not having been paid, stand satisfied.
